## TL;DR
Task branches now contain only their own task's files. The engineer self-check checkpoint commit stages only the task's own files plus source changes, handoff restores other tasks' `work/` and `work/reports/` files from main before the review lock, and the landing preflight names the offending files and cause in plain English.

## Work and rationale
An audit of the server paths that can write another task's bookkeeping into a task worktree found the WIP checkpoint commit (blanket staging) and the merge-of-main sync as the leak points. The checkpoint commit now excludes `work/*.md` for other ids and `work/reports/<other id>/**`, with the pathspec kept inside #1082's wait-for-check-release wrapper. Handoff restores sibling files from main through a normal commit review tolerates, and reports what it restored. Hotfix, union-merge and report commits are pathspec-scoped. `repoos landable` and the handoff report name the files and cause. Tests cover a dirty worktree producing a clean checkpoint, a drifted branch healed at handoff, and the preflight passing afterwards; docs describe the rule.

## Approaches tried
Manual per-round restores (the old way), then blocking the leak at the source and healing drift at handoff.

## Challenges and blockers
Handoffs collided with the engineer's own check, a recorded identical check failure blocked an unchanged tip, and #1082 landing in the same files caused a merge conflict that was resolved by merging main and keeping the pathspec inside the wait callback.

## Key learnings
Fix the source of the leak and heal drift at handoff. A handoff on an unchanged tip needs a new commit, and conflicts with a just-landed task should be resolved by merging main early.
